Which Muslim kingdom came into existence after the disintegration of the Bahmani Empire?
x: The Bahmani kingdom split into five: Adil Shahi (Bijapur), Nizam Shahi (Ahmednagar), Qutb Shahi (Golconda), Barid Shahi (Bidar) and Imad Shahi (Berar).

s: Who founded the Hyderabad State?
x:
Sultan Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, the fifth ruler of the Qutb Shahi dynasty, founded the city of Hyderabad in 1591 CE. He shifted the capital from Golconda to the newly built city of Hyderabad and constructed famous monuments such as the Charminar. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:
• Founder of Hyderabad City – Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah
• Year – 1591 CE

s: Who founded the city of Bhagyanagar?
x: Bhagyanagar, the older name associated with Hyderabad, is traditionally linked to Mohammed Quli Qutub Shah, who founded the city in the late 16th century. The city was reportedly named after Bhagmati and later renamed Hyderabad.

s: Choose the pair which is not correctly matched.
x: Yusuf Adil Shah founded the Adil Shahi dynasty of Bijapur, not Ahmadnagar (the Nizam Shahi capital, founded by Malik Ahmad). So the pair is wrongly matched; the other pairs are correct.

s:
Match the following.
List I (Dynasty)
List II (Sultanate formed after disintegration of Deccan Sultanate)

B. Barid Shahi
2. Berar

C. Imad Shahi
3. Bidar

D. Nizam Shahi

s: Which of the following is not true about Gol Gumbaz?
o: It is the tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah.
There is no mosque and no arches near the tomb.
Its dome is one of the largest in the world.
x:
Gol Gumbaz, located at Bijapur (Vijayapura) in Karnataka, is the magnificent mausoleum of Muhammad Adil Shah, the seventh ruler of the Adil Shahi dynasty. It is famous for:
• One of the world's largest masonry domes
• The famous Whispering Gallery
• Impressive arches and surrounding architectural structures Therefore, the statement that there is no mosque and no arches near the tomb is incorrect. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Gol Gumbaz → Bijapur
• Tomb of → Muhammad Adil Shah

s: The famous diamond ‘Kohinoor’ was presented to Shah Jahan by –
x: The Kohinoor Diamond, one of the famous diamonds in the world, was discovered in the mines of Golconda. Mir Jumla was a minister of Sultan of Golconda, Abdullah Qutub Shah (1626-1672 A.D.) who got angry over Mir Jumla for accepting the Mansab of King Shah Jahan and seized all his property. Later, Shah Jahan sent Aurangzeb to attack Golconda, and the matter was resolved, and the treaty was signed between them. Later, Mir Jumla was called back to Agra and given the title of “Muazzam Khan.” Mir Jumla, the Persian noble and a reputed diamond dealer, visited the court of Shah Jahan and presented the Kohinoor diamond to the Mughal emperor.

s: Who among the following had presented the famous ‘Kohinoor’ diamond to Shah Jahan?
x: Mir Jumla, minister of Abdullah Qutb Shah, gave the Kohinoor to Shah Jahan; Tavernier only recorded it.

x: The Kohinoor came from Kollur, a mine in the Golconda kingdom's territory on the Krishna, so Golconda is the best option here; Bijapur is wrong.

s: Which one of the following Muslim rulers was hailed as the 'Jagadguru' by his Muslim subjects because of his belief in secularism?
x: Ibrahim Adil Shah II of Bijapur (1580–1627) was known for his broad-minded and syncretic outlook. He patronised Hindu scholars, participated in Hindu cultural traditions, and composed devotional works that reflected both Islamic and Hindu influences (e.g., Kitab-i-Navras). Because of his inclusive and secular approach, he was hailed as 'Jagadguru' by his subjects.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Kitab‑i‑Nauras, a collection of songs in praise of Hindu deities and Muslim saints, was written by Ibrahim Adil Shah II.
2. Amir Khusrau was the originator in India of the early form of the musical style known as Qawwali. Which of these statements is/are correct?
x: The Kitab-i-Nauras or the Book of Nine Rasas consist of fifty-nine songs and seventeen couplets composed by Sultan Ibrahim Adil Shah II of Bijapur. The Kitab-i-Nauras Blends Hindu and Islamic devotion through Poetry and Music, Celebrating Deities Like Saraswati and Ganesha alongside Islamic Figures such as Prophet Hazrat Muhammad and Hazrat Khwaja Bande Nawaz. Amir Khusrau is regarded as the pioneer of qawwali in the Indian subcontinent. Associated with the Chishti Sufi tradition, he introduced the qaul style and blended Persian, Hindavi, and Sufi poetic elements to shape the early form of qawwali.
